chapter_seo_title: Mortal’s Journey Chapter 341: Han Li’s Ultimate Assassin’s Patience with the Heart-Boring Worm
chapter_meta_description: Han Li plants a slow-kill worm on a treacherous mortal, tracks a freshly awakened Qu Hun, and discovers the bitter truth about Zhang Tie’s lost talent.
og_title: The Worm that Waits a Year: Han Li’s Coldest Calculated Murder
og_description: In a masterclass of the Mortal Stream, Han Li uses a parasite that takes a full year to kill an enemy, ensuring perfect deniability and a chilling fulfillment of a promise.
twitter_title: Han Li’s “Goodbye” Slap is a Death Sentence
twitter_description: Did Han Li just fulfill a promise by planting a heart-boring worm in a mortal leader? Yes. Yes he did.

lore_anchors.definition: One of the Seven Great Sects of the Yue Kingdom, known for its spirit beast taming and control arts.
A ritual artifact used to bind and command soulless bodies; it contains a trace of its target’s essence blood for tracking.
A parasitic insect nearly invisible to the naked eye, used for slow, perfectly disguised assassinations; it crawls to the heart over a period of years, mimicking a natural heart attack.
A cultivator’s most vital life force; permanently depleted upon use, causing irreversible damage to lifespan and cultivation base.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li kill the sect leader over a *thought*?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Han Li doesn't just kill for actions; he kills for potential future threats. Seeing the leader's duplicity, he pre-emptively removes the risk of being informed on with a failsafe that provides perfect deniability.

cultural_notes_faq.q: How does Qu Hun suddenly have Spiritual Roots?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Zhang Tie (Qu Hun's original body) lacked wood-attribute Spiritual Roots for the Eternal Spring Art but possessed an entirely different, viable Spirit Root, which the reawakened puppet can now utilize.
